verdict: The export contains 308 frames across 12.8 seconds. Full playback quality and frame intervals are recorded above.
boundaries: This is a headless Chromium decoder test, not a measurement of the user sidebar GPU or its live Three.js rendering speed.
getVideoPlaybackQuality measures playback drops; it cannot recover scene frames that were never encoded.
Frame count and timestamps were independently read from the saved WebM with ffprobe. The stream r_frame_rate field is not a reliable average for this variable frame rate file.
The average frame rate uses the actual browser playback duration; the container declared duration is separately recorded because it can differ from the packet timeline.
requestVideoFrameCallback is an observed compositor callback count, not the encoded frame count; headless compositor callbacks can be fewer than the playback quality total.
Audio byte counters establish decoding, not subjective sound quality or gap-free audio; packet timestamps are recorded for further inspection.
